newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to see 96 farm deficit vs surplus 95 - CNA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to see 96 farm deficit vs surplus 95 - CNA.

text.p: Mexico will record a farm trade balance deficit in 1996 of $1.4 billion reversing a surplus in 1995 of $764 million, the National Farm Council said Wednesday in a year end report.
"This situation is explained mainly because of grain and oilseed purchases in the first half of the year that were at extraordinarily high prices," the CNA said.

"On the other hand, the value of our exports could not hold the rhythm of growth recorded in 1995 because of the drop in international coffee prices and some fruit and vegetables as well as the decrease in livestock head," it added.

The CNA said the decrease in livestock exports came primarily because of the fall in the national stocks. Exports boomed in 1995 as a drought swept northern states, forcing cattlemen to export or watch animals die, drastically lowering the number of head in Mexico.

"For 1997, we expect a growth in the farm gross domestic product (GDP) of between 2 and 2.5 percent, a farm trade balance in the balance, or with a slight deficit of $200 million," it added. "In 1997, we see imports of grains around 5.2 million tonnes, including corn, wheat, sorghum, barley, rice and dry beans," the CNA said..
